title: U.S. House · Maine's 2nd District
area: Northern, western, and central Maine, including Lewiston, Bangor, and Aroostook County — geographically most of the state outside greater Portland.

context.text: Incumbent Jared Golden (D), first elected in 2018, did not seek re-election, leaving the seat open for the first time since 2014.

Donald Trump carried the 2nd District 53.5%-44.5% over Kamala Harris in 2024, while Golden won re-election in the district 50.3%-49.7% the same year; Republicans consider the open seat a pickup opportunity in 2026.

Matthew Dunlap defeated Joe Baldacci, Paige Loud, and Jordan Wood in the Democratic primary. Paul LePage, Maine's former governor, won the Republican primary unopposed after James Clark did not make the ballot.

summary.text: Matthew Dunlap is the Democratic nominee for Maine's 2nd Congressional District. He is the sitting Maine State Auditor and previously served as Maine Secretary of State and in the Maine House of Representatives.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in history and a master's degree in literature from the University of Maine.
Served as Maine Secretary of State (2005-2011 and 2013-2021) and in the Maine House of Representatives, District 121 (1996-2004).
Worked in publishing, food service, and non-profit executive roles before his current tenure as Maine State Auditor (since 2022, with a brief prior stint in 2021).

priorities.text: Says he is running to stand up to the Trump administration and to fight for affordable healthcare, a lower cost of living, and higher wages.
priorities.quote: Mainers deserve a fighter who won't cave to Donald Trump. ... When I'm in Congress, I'll stand up for Maine, and I'll fight for affordable healthcare, a lower cost of living, and higher wages for hardworking people.

priorities.text: On healthcare, says he wants to re-establish ACA tax credits but sees Medicare for All as the broader goal.
priorities.quote: re-establish [ACA] tax credits, but overall, I think the real answer is Medicare-for-All and just cut to the chase.

positions.summary: Supports restoring ACA tax credits in the near term and says Medicare for All is the longer-term goal.
positions.quote: re-establish [ACA] tax credits, but overall, I think the real answer is Medicare-for-All and just cut to the chase.

record.text: Elected Maine State Auditor in 2022 (with a brief earlier appointment in 2021); the position audits state government finances.
Served as Maine Secretary of State from 2005-2011 and 2013-2021.

summary.text: Paul LePage is the Republican nominee for Maine's 2nd Congressional District. He served two terms as Governor of Maine (2011-2019) and previously as Mayor of Waterville.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration in finance/accounting from Husson University and an M.B.A. from the University of Maine.
Served as Mayor of Waterville, Maine (2004-2011) and was general manager of Marden's Surplus and Salvage.
Served two terms as Governor of Maine (2011-2019).

priorities.text: Campaigns on his record as governor, citing a lower unemployment rate, reduced state spending, addressing hospital debt, the state's largest tax cut, welfare reform, and increased K-12 spending.
Says he would help end wasteful federal spending and secure the border, while protecting Social Security and Medicare.
priorities.quote: I'll help President Trump end waste and fraud and secure our borders. Let's lower the cost of electricity and everyday items by ending Biden's inflation policies, bring our northern Maine economy back, help end the woke extremism — putting boys in girls sports, protect our freedoms like the Second Amendment, secure our hospitals ... [and] always protect social security and Medicare.

positions.summary: Says he would protect Second Amendment freedoms.
positions.quote: protect our freedoms like the Second Amendment

record.text: As Governor of Maine (2011-2019), his campaign says he lowered the state's unemployment rate, reduced state spending, addressed hospital debt, implemented what he describes as the state's largest tax cut, and reformed welfare.
